Born Saloth Sâr, this Maoist dictator led the Khmer Rouge to power in 1975, presiding over a genocide that killed roughly a quarter of his country's population. Who is he?
As second son and designated heir apparent to Iraq's dictator from 2000, this security official ran the Republican Guard and reportedly authorized torture against dissidents — who was he?
Widely considered the greatest mountaineer ever, who made the first solo ascent of Everest and was the first to climb all fourteen eight-thousanders without supplemental oxygen?
Reinhold Messner: Italian mountaineer, adventurer and explorer (born 1944)

Born when Octavian rose to power and established the Augustan Principate in 27 BC, its western half fell in 476 AD while its eastern half lived on until Constantinople fell in 1453. What state is this?
Roman Empire: 27 BC–476/1453 AD state and civilization. The Roman Empire was a state that dominated the Mediterranean and much of Europe, Western Asia, and North Africa during the classical period.
After losing three presidential bids, this Chilean socialist finally won in 1970 — often called the first Marxist elected president in a liberal democracy in Latin America. Who was he?
Salvador Allende: President of Chile from 1970 to 1973.
A member of Japan's Liberal Democratic Party, this politician served as Deputy Chief Cabinet Secretary and State Minister for Foreign Affairs under the Third Abe Cabinet — who is he?
Discovered hiding in Guam's jungle in 1972, this Japanese army sergeant was one of the last WWII holdouts found nearly three decades after the fighting ended — who was he?
Shoichi Yokoi: Japanese World War II holdout (1915–1997)
This mythical creature combines a human head with a lion's body — in Greek myth she poses a fatal riddle to Oedipus, while in Egyptian tradition it's an unwinged, benevolent guardian — what is it?

Sphinx: Mythological creature with a human head and lion body. In Greek tradition, the sphinx is a treacherous and merciless being with the head of a woman, the haunches of a lion, and the wings of a bird.
Appointed by Emmanuel Macron in September 2025 after the previous government fell to a no-confidence vote, this politician had previously served as France's minister of the armed forces — who is he?
Sébastien Lecornu: Prime Minister of France since 2025.
Serving as UK Home Secretary before becoming the country's second female Prime Minister in 2016, this Conservative politician represented Maidenhead in Parliament for over two decades — who is she?
Theresa May: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom from 2016 to 2019.

Walled off to the east and south by the Carpathians and to the west by the Apuseni Mountains, this historical region sits in central Romania and goes by Erdély in Hungarian and Siebenbürgen in German. What is it?
Transylvania: Historical region in Central Europe. Broader definitions of Transylvania also include the western and northwestern Romanian regions of Crișana and Maramureș, and occasionally Banat.
This Mexican revolutionary-turned-president oversaw the drafting of the 1917 constitution and kept his country neutral in World War I before being assassinated in 1920 — who is he?
Venustiano Carranza: President of Mexico from 1914 to 1920.
This Kenyan activist founded the tree-planting Green Belt Movement and in 2004 became the first African woman to win the Nobel Peace Prize. Who was she?
Called the 'father of modern Liberia,' he was the country's longest-serving president, drawing foreign investment and pursuing national unification from 1944 until his death in 1971 — who is he?
William Tubman: President of Liberia from 1944 to 1971. William Vacanarat Shadrach Tubman (29 November 1895 – 23 July 1971) was a Liberian politician.
A labour lawyer and longtime Communist Party member, which Spanish politician founded the left-wing alliance Sumar and serves as Second Deputy Prime Minister?
Yolanda Díaz: Spanish politician and lawyer (born 1971)
Which of these people was born first?
Ada Lovelace (born 1815) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is the eldest?

Omar Khayyam (born 1048) is the earliest of the four. Omar Khayyam (1048–1131) was a Persian poet and polymath, known for his contributions to mathematics, astronomy, philosophy, and Persian literature.
Who among these was born first?
Havelock Ellis (born 1859) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four began earliest?
Assembly language (founded 1949) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is an astronomer?
Who among these is a mathematician?
Leonhard Euler is a mathematician. Euler has been called a "universal genius" who "was fully equipped with almost unlimited powers of imagination, intellectual gifts and extraordinary memory".
Pick the chemist from these four.
Maud Menten is a chemist. Maud Leonora Menten (March 20, 1879 – July 17, 1960) was a Canadian physician and chemist.
What is the atomic number of Silicon?
Silicon (SILL-ih-kən) is a chemical element; it has symbol Si and atomic number 14.
In what year was Jerry Buss born?
Jerry Buss: Gerald Hatten Buss (January 27, 1933 – February 18, 2013) was an American businessman, investor, chemist, and philanthropist.
In what year was Pierre Curie born?
Pierre Curie (15 May 1859 – 19 April 1906) was a French physicist and chemist, and a pioneer in crystallography and magnetism.
In what year was Kevin Mitnick born?
Kevin Mitnick: Kevin David Mitnick (August 6, 1963 – July 16, 2023) was an American computer security consultant, author, and convicted hacker.
In what year did John von Neumann die?
John von Neumann: During World War II, von Neumann worked on the Manhattan Project.
In what year did C. V. Raman die?
C. V. Raman: This phenomenon, a hitherto unknown type of scattering of light they called modified scattering, was subsequently termed the Raman effect or Raman scattering.
In what year was Euler's formula discovered?
Euler's formula: The formula is still valid if x is a complex number, and is also called Euler's formula in this more general case.
COBOL: CODASYL. COBOL (Common Business-Oriented Language;) is a compiled English-like computer programming language designed for business use.
Propofol: Pfizer. Propofol is the active component of an intravenous anesthetic used for induction and maintenance of general anesthesia.
Boxer (dog breed): German Empire. The Boxer is a medium to large, short-haired dog breed of mastiff-type, developed in Germany.
Who is credited with discovering Special relativity?
Special relativity: Albert Einstein. In physics, the special theory of relativity, or simply special relativity, is a scientific theory of the relationship between space and time.
Who is credited with discovering Carbon dioxide?
Carbon dioxide: Jan Baptist van Helmont. Carbon dioxide is a chemical compound with the chemical formula CO2.
Who is credited with discovering Calcium?
Calcium: Humphry Davy. Calcium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ca and atomic number 20.
Made of adenine bonded to a sugar, this RNA building block underlies ATP, the cell's main energy currency, and doubles as an IV treatment for certain cardiac arrhythmias — what is it?
Adenosine (symbol A) is an organic compound that occurs widely in nature in the form of diverse derivatives.
The simplest pnictogen hydride, with the formula NH3, this pungent gas is also a common nitrogenous waste in living things — what is it?
Ammonia is an inorganic chemical compound of nitrogen and hydrogen with the formula NH3.
This Portuguese economist-turned-dictator ruled as head of government from 1932 to 1968, rebranding his authoritarian regime as the corporatist 'New State.' Who is he?
António de Oliveira Salazar (28 April 1889 - 27 July 1970) was a Portuguese dictator, academic, and economist who served as President of the Council of Ministers of Portugal from 1932 to 1968.
Once native to the highland lakes of Xochimilco and Chalco, this neotenic mole salamander keeps its external gills and stays aquatic for life — what is it?
Axolotl (from Classical; Ambystoma mexicanum) is a species of mole salamander.
What yellow-green digestive fluid is produced continuously by the liver but stored and concentrated in the gallbladder until it's needed to break down fats in the small intestine?
Bile (from Latin bilis), also known as gall, is a yellow-green fluid produced by the liver of most vertebrates that aids the digestion of lipids in the small intestine.

Making up only about 2.6 percent of the brain's total weight, this stalk-like structure connects the cerebrum to the spinal cord and regulates critical functions like heart rate and breathing. What is it called?
Brainstem (or brain stem) is the posterior stalk-like part of the brain that connects the cerebrum with the spinal cord.
This biological family includes domestic dogs, wolves, coyotes, foxes, and jackals, found on every continent except Antarctica. What family is it?
Canidae (from Latin, canis, "dog") is a biological family of caniform carnivorans, constituting a clade.
Despite no clinical evidence it treats any disease, this daisy-like plant is a staple in calming herbal tea, beer brewing, and even garden ground cover — what is it?
Chamomile (American English) or camomile (British English; see spelling differences) (or) is the common name for several daisy-like plants of the family Asteraceae.
This neurological disorder strikes one side of the head around the eye and temple, often at the very same hour each day for an 8-to-10-week stretch before vanishing for months — what condition is it?
Cluster headache is a neurological disorder characterized by episodes of severe headaches on one side of the head, typically around the eye and temple, lasting between 15 minutes to three hours.
Which genus of passerine birds, whose Latin name literally means 'raven,' includes about 46 species commonly known as crows, ravens, and rooks?
Corvus is a widely distributed genus of passerine birds ranging from medium-sized to large-sized in the family Corvidae.
Affecting some 280 million people worldwide, this state of low mood saps motivation and the pleasure once taken in activities — what is it?
Depression (mood) is a mental state of low mood and aversion to activity.
Covering everything from a fibrous bone condition to a kidney disorder, this term for abnormal tissue growth is usually precancerous rather than outright malignant — what is it?

Dysplasia is any of various types of abnormal growth or development of cells (microscopic scale) or organs (macroscopic scale), and the abnormal histology or anatomical structure(s) resulting from such growth.
This thin, protective tissue type lines the outer surfaces of organs and the inner surfaces of blood vessels; the skin's outermost layer is a familiar example. What is it?
Epithelium is a thin, continuous, protective layer of cells with little extracellular matrix.

Likely domesticated from the European polecat, with which it can still interbreed, this slender Mustelid pet weighs up to about two kilograms and comes in coats of black, brown or white — which animal?
Ferret (Mustela furo) is a small, domesticated species belonging to the family Mustelidae.
Caused by a loss of blood supply, this type of tissue death most commonly affects the feet and hands and can turn skin red or black. What condition is it?
Gangrene is a type of tissue death caused by a lack of blood supply. If the gangrene is caused by an infectious agent, it may present with a fever or sepsis.
This term describes the overall system of processes, rules, and power structures that sets boundaries of conduct and steers the direction of an organized group — what is it?

Governance is the overall complex system or framework of processes, functions, structures, rules, laws and norms born out of the relationships, interactions, power dynamics and communication within an organized group of individuals.

His synergy with information-theory father Claude Shannon laid foundations for the Information Age, and during WWII he helped build automatic guns that defended London from V-1 flying bombs — who was this Dutch-American control-theory pioneer?
Hendrik Wade Bode (-d,; December 24, 1905 - June 21, 1982) was an American engineer, researcher, inventor, author and scientist, of Dutch ancestry.
This thin piece of mucosal tissue that surrounds or partially covers the vaginal opening takes its name from a Greek word meaning 'thin skin' — name the structure?
Hymen is a thin piece of mucosal tissue that surrounds or partially covers the vaginal opening. It forms part of the vulva and is similar in structure to the vagina.
One of the largest dog breeds in the world, this sighthound was historically used to course game and became the official mascot of a British Guards regiment in 1902. What breed is it?
Irish Wolfhound is a breed of large sighthound that has, by its presence and substantial size, inspired literature, poetry and mythology.
Originally trained as a mathematician, this English economist built the foundation for an entire school of macroeconomic thought that bears his name — who is he?

John Maynard Keynes (KAYNZ; 5 June 1883 - 21 April 1946), was an English economist whose writings are considered the basis for the school of thought known as Keynesian economics, as well as its various offshoots.
Native to southern China but long cultivated in Japan and Southeast Asia, this small fruit closely resembles an orange in color and texture but is only about the size of a large olive — what is it?
Kumquat are a group of small, angiosperm, fruit-bearing trees in the family Rutaceae.

First isolated from linseed oil and named from the Latin words for 'flax' and 'oil,' this omega-6 polyunsaturated fatty acid is one of the two essential fats humans must get from their diet — which acid?
Linoleic acid (LA) is an organic compound with the formula CH3(CH2)4CH=CHCH2CH=CH(CH2)7COOH.

A chemical element with symbol Mg and atomic number 12, it's a shiny gray metal with low density and high chemical reactivity that readily reacts with air to form a thin passivation oxide coating. What element is this?
Magnesium is a chemical element; it has symbol Mg and atomic number 12. The free metal burns with a brilliant-white light.
Most common on the legs in women and the back in men, this cancer develops from melanin-producing skin cells and, in extremely rare cases, can even arise in the lungs — which cancer?
Melanoma is a type of cancer, typically skin cancer; it develops from the melanin-producing cells known as melanocytes.
This small, subterranean mammal has velvety fur, tiny eyes, and short powerful forelimbs with oversized paws built for constant digging — what animal is it?

It's the inherent character of the universe as a whole — the laws, elements, and phenomena of the physical world, including life itself — even though humans are often spoken of as somehow apart from it. What is it?
Nature is an inherent character or constitution, particularly of the ecosphere or the universe as a whole.

Classified using a measurement of weight divided by the square of height, this medical condition is diagnosed when that figure exceeds 30 and is linked to cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes — what is it?
Obesity is a medical condition, considered a disease by multiple organizations, in which excess body fat has accumulated to such an extent that it can have negative effects on health.

This genus of 70 to 100 frost-tolerant annual, biennial, and perennial species native to temperate Eurasia, Africa, and North America is the type genus of its flowering plant family — what's the genus?
Papaver is a genus of 70-100 species of frost-tolerant annuals, biennials, and perennials native to temperate and cold regions of Eurasia, Africa and North America.
Its Nahuatl-derived name means 'caterpillar cocoon,' and this small, spineless desert cactus native to northern Mexico and south Texas contains the psychoactive alkaloid mescaline — what's the plant?
Peyote is a small, spineless cactus which contains psychoactive alkaloids, particularly mescaline.
This inflammation of the lining around the lungs causes sharp chest pain that worsens with breathing, and is most often triggered by a viral infection — what condition is it?
Pleurisy is inflammation of the membranes that surround the lungs and line the chest cavity (pleurae).
Classified into acute, chronic, and pelvic pain syndrome subtypes, this condition doesn't always match its name's literal meaning of organ swelling — which condition?
Prostatitis is an umbrella term for a variety of medical conditions that incorporate bacterial and non-bacterial origin illnesses in the pelvic region.

The largest of the true foxes and the most widely distributed carnivore on Earth, it spread alongside human settlement so successfully that, after being introduced to Australia, it landed on the list of the world's 100 worst invasive species. Which animal is it?
Red fox (Vulpes vulpes) is the largest of the true foxes, and the most widely distributed member of the order Carnivora.
Enforcing memory safety without a garbage collector through something called a 'borrow checker,' this general-purpose language blends functional and object-oriented paradigms — which language?
Rust (programming language) is a general-purpose programming language which emphasizes performance, type safety, concurrency, and memory safety.
This taxonomic order groups cephalopods distinguished by having ten arms instead of eight — what order is it?
Sepiida is an order of ten-armed cephalopods.
This plant family includes both deadly poisonous species and kitchen staples like tomatoes, potatoes, and peppers, all linked by unusually high alkaloid content — what family is it?
Solanaceae is a family of flowering plants in the order Solanales.
This colorless, sweet-smelling liquid with the formula C6H5CH=CH2 is manufactured from benzene as the industrial precursor to a widely used plastic — what compound is it?
Styrene is an organic compound with the chemical formula C6H5CH=CH2.

The primary male sex hormone and androgen, this hormone plays a key role in developing male reproductive tissues and secondary sexual characteristics like muscle, bone mass, and body hair. What is this hormone?

Testosterone is the primary male sex hormone and androgen in males. It is associated with increased aggression, sex drive, dominance, courtship display, and a wide range of behavioral characteristics.

Caused by the parasite Toxoplasma gondii and often spread through undercooked meat or contact with infected cat feces, this disease can be especially dangerous to a developing baby if a woman is infected during pregnancy — what is it?
Toxoplasmosis is a parasitic disease caused by Toxoplasma gondii, an apicomplexan.
Just 25 light-years away, this is the brightest star in the constellation Lyra and the fifth-brightest star in the entire night sky — what is it?
Vega is the brightest star in the northern constellation of Lyra. It has the Bayer designation α Lyrae, which is Latinised to Alpha Lyrae and abbreviated Alpha Lyr or α Lyr.
Inspired by the code-breaking game Mastermind, this once-a-day puzzle gives you six tries and colored tiles to crack the same word everyone else is solving — which game?
The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom
Wordle is a web-based word game created and developed by the Welsh software engineer Josh Wardle.
The simplest and smallest ketone, this colorless, pungent, highly flammable liquid mixes freely with water and lurks in nail polish remover and paint thinner — what is it?
Working at Baghdad's House of Wisdom around 820, this Islamic Golden Age scholar wrote a treatise whose Arabic title, Al-Jabr, gave us the very word "algebra." Who was he?
Sometimes called 'pigweed,' this genus of plants is grown worldwide as a leaf vegetable and for its edible grain — which genus?
Amaranth: Genus of plants. The plant can grow from 1 to 2.5 metres (3 to 8 feet) tall with a succulent, hollow stem.
Comprising the talocrural, subtalar, and inferior tibiofibular joints, this region where the foot meets the leg enables dorsiflexion and plantarflexion — which body part?
Ankle: Region where the foot and the leg meet. The ankle includes three joints: the ankle joint proper or talocrural joint, the subtalar joint, and the inferior tibiofibular joint.
The clinging seed burrs of this plant genus, commonly known as burdock, directly inspired the invention of the hook-and-loop fastener — which genus?
This independent examination of financial records culminates in a report expressing an opinion on whether the books are free of material misstatement — what is it called?
Audit: Independent examination of an organization. The term is most frequently applied to audits of the financial information relating to a legal person.
Produced continuously from 1964 to 2021, this line of twin-turboprop utility aircraft outsold all of its turboprop rivals combined — which aircraft family?
Beechcraft King Air: Twin engine turboprop aircraft family. The King Air line comprises a number of twin-turboprop models that have been divided into two families.

Despite its name, this snake is actually grey to dark brown — the name instead describes the dark interior of its mouth, displayed as a threat — which species, the second-longest venomous snake after the king cobra?
Black mamba: Species of venomous snake. The black mamba (Dendroaspis polylepis) is a species of highly venomous snake belonging to the family Elapidae.
Cattle, bison, buffalo, and goat-antelopes like sheep and goats all belong to this family of cloven-hoofed ruminants with over 140 living species — what is it?
Bovidae: Family of mammals belonging to even-toed ungulates.
Historically hardware-dependent in size, ranging anywhere from 1 to 48 bits, this unit of digital information now almost always means eight bits — what's it called?
Byte: Unit of digital information, usually 8 bits.
With the formula H2CO3, this fleeting compound has a lifespan of only about 20 milliseconds at body temperature before converting to water and carbon dioxide — which compound?
Carbonic acid: Chemical compound. The molecule rapidly converts to water and carbon dioxide in the presence of water.
Nicknamed 'no-see-ums' for their tiny 1-3mm size, these biting midges are also among the best-studied pollinators of cocoa plants — what is this fly family called?
Ceratopogonidae: Family of flies commonly known as no see ums, or biting midges.
Usually triggered when a gallstone blocks the cystic duct, this inflammatory condition causes right-upper abdominal pain that radiates to the shoulder — what is it?
Their 'lady' actually refers to the Virgin Mary, and their cheerful red-and-black warning colours tell predators they taste terrible — what is this 6,000-species family of small beetles?
Coccinellidae: Family of beetles. The more than 6,000 described species have a global distribution and are found in a variety of habitats.
First created near Darmstadt in 1996 and named for an astronomer on his 537th anniversary, this synthetic element (number 112) is so volatile it may even be a gas — which element?
Copernicium: Chemical element with atomic number 112 (Cn)
First flown in 1938 and built almost 14,000 strong at a factory in Buffalo, New York, this WWII fighter-bomber was known to British and Soviet pilots as the Tomahawk or Kittyhawk — which aircraft?
Curtiss P-40 Warhawk: American WWII fighter. The Curtiss P-40 Warhawk is an American single-engined, single-seat, all-metal fighter-bomber that first flew in 1938.
Spread by mosquitoes in tropical regions, this virus is often mild but can turn severe with bleeding, plummeting platelet counts, and dangerously low blood pressure — what is it?
Synthesized from L-DOPA in the brain and kidneys, this catecholamine acts as a neurotransmitter and drives a major brain pathway tied to reward and motivation — what is it?
Dopamine: Organic chemical that functions both as a hormone and a neurotransmitter.
Known as aubergine or brinjal elsewhere, this purple, spongy fruit in the nightshade family is technically a berry despite usually being cooked as a vegetable — what is it?
A German Jew who fled the Nazi regime, this social psychologist and democratic socialist helped found a psychoanalytic institute in New York and was linked to the Frankfurt School — who is he?
Once widespread during the Pleistocene and later reintroduced by humans to its ancient range, which hoofed mammal species is native to Turkey and possibly Italy, the Balkans, and Rhodes?
European fallow deer: Species of hooved mammal. The European fallow deer (Dama dama), also known as the common fallow deer or simply fallow deer, is a species of deer native to Eurasia.
Known as the weeping fig and the official tree of Bangkok, this flowering plant native to Asia and Australia is often used as a biomonitor in cities — which species?
Ficus benjamina: Species of fig. The species is also naturalized in the West Indies and in the states of Florida and Arizona in the United States.
Before becoming Ferrari's Formula One team principal in 2023, this Frenchman co-founded a junior-racing outfit that won back-to-back titles with Lewis Hamilton and Nico Rosberg — who is he?
Called 'a bridge between the natural and social sciences,' this discipline studies Earth's lands, features, inhabitants, and how they all came to be — what is it?
Geography: Study of Earth's spatial information.
This common name covers edible fruit from the Ribes genus — the same genus as currants — coming in colors from green and red to purple, yellow, white, or black — which fruit?
Gooseberry: Species of Ribes cultivated for its edible fruit.
Producing up to a hundred billion new cells a day from specialized stem cells, this biological process manufactures every component of blood — what is it?
Haematopoiesis: Formation of blood cellular components.

Many people show no symptoms after catching this liver-attacking virus, but when signs do appear weeks later they can include nausea, yellowing skin, and fatigue — and an infection lasting past six months is deemed chronic. What is it?

Drawing on anthropology, paleontology and genetics, this field studies how our species gradually gained bipedalism, dexterity and complex language — and shows our past was weblike, with interbreeding among archaic humans — what is the subject?
Human evolution: Homo sapiens is a distinct species of the hominid family of primates, which includes all the great apes.

This crystalline mineral form of frozen water occurs naturally on Earth, other planets, and even in Oort cloud objects, and has at least nineteen known phases depending on temperature and pressure — what is it?
Ice: Frozen water; the solid state of water.
This purplish-black Brazilian fruit doesn't dangle from branches — it sprouts straight out of the tree trunk itself. What is it?
Jabuticaba: Tree in the family Myrtaceae.
Credited with popularizing the index fund, this investor founded The Vanguard Group and preached long-term patience over speculation — who is he?
John C. Bogle: American investor and business magnate (1929–2019)
This NMDA-receptor-blocking anesthetic induces a trance-like dissociative state while preserving breathing and raising blood pressure, and at lower doses treats resistant depression — which drug?
At Bologna in the 1700s she became the first woman to hold a science doctorate and the first salaried female university teacher — depicted as the goddess Minerva herself; who was she?
Laura Bassi: Italian physicist and academic (1711–1778)
This soft, movable pair of appendages on the jaw helps with eating and speech, and is often used in kissing — what are they?
Lip: Visible body parts at the mouth.
Named from the Latin for "wolf," this autoimmune disease often announces itself with a red facial rash and alternates between flares and remission — what is it?
Lupus: Autoimmune disease in which the immune system attacks healthy tissue.
Boiled down from its sap to make a beloved breakfast syrup, this genus of roughly 132 tree and shrub species counts the sycamore as its type species — which genus of trees?

Fever, a fierce headache, neck stiffness, and a telltale rash that doesn't fade when a glass is rolled over it can signal this inflammation of the membranes around the brain and spinal cord — what is it?

Meningitis: Inflammation of membranes around the brain. Meningitis (pl. meningitides) is acute or chronic inflammation of the protective membranes covering the brain and spinal cord, collectively called the meninges.

An advanced modification of its Korean War-era predecessor, this Soviet transonic fighter — NATO reporting name 'Fresco' — was license-built in China and Poland, and remains in North Korean service today — which jet?
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-17: Soviet jet fighter aircraft family.
Nicknamed noni, this pungent-smelling fruit tree in the coffee family was spread across the Pacific by Polynesian sailors and is now used mainly in traditional medicine and juices — which plant?
Morinda citrifolia: Species of plant. It is commonly known as noni or Indian mulberry, among many other names.
Made of two fused benzene rings, this pungent white crystalline compound is the main ingredient in traditional mothballs — what is it?
Naphthalene: Chemical compound. It is a white crystalline solid with a characteristic odor that is detectable at concentrations as low as 0.08 ppm.
Known informally as bedwetting, this involuntary condition rarely stems from a specific medical cause and is often treated with alarms or hormone therapy — what is it called medically?
Nocturnal enuresis: Involuntary urination while asleep.
This biological process turns a primary oocyte into an egg cell capable of developing once fertilized, beginning during embryonic development — what is it called?
Oogenesis: Egg cell production process. Oogenesis or ovogenesis is the differentiation of the ovum (egg cell) into a cell competent to further develop when fertilized.
Sold under the brand name Protonix, this proton-pump inhibitor treats ulcers and acid reflux but can, with long-term use, cause vitamin B12 deficiency and low magnesium — what is this drug?
Native to Asia, Europe, and western North America, this flowering shrub's fragrant blooms last just 7 to 10 days each spring — which plant?
Peony: Genus of flowering plants in the family Paeoniaceae.
Known across South Asia as Indian gooseberry or amla, this deciduous tree is native to tropical regions of the continent — which plant?
Phyllanthus emblica: Berry and plant. Phyllanthus emblica, commonly known as emblic, Indian gooseberry, amalaki, amloki, or amla, is a deciduous tree of the family Phyllanthaceae.

The most common hormonal disorder in women of reproductive age, it's diagnosed by two of three signs — irregular periods, high testosterone, or many antral follicles — despite a name that misleadingly implies true cysts. What's its newer name?
Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome: Hormonal disorder in women. The exact cause of PMOS remains uncertain.
Native to Eurasia and known by the common names 'cherry plum' and 'myrobalan plum,' this species is thought to be a parent of the cultivated plum — what is it, scientifically?
Prunus cerasifera: Species of plum. Native to Eurasia and naturalized elsewhere, P. cerasifera is believed to be one of the parents of the cultivated plum.
Built from bases including uracil, adenine, guanine, and cytosine, this molecule can serve as a template for building proteins or catalyze reactions itself — what is it?
RNA: Family of large biological molecules.
One of the largest land megafauna left, this odd-toed ungulate has five surviving species — two in Africa, three across South and Southeast Asia — and a name meaning "nose-horned." What is it?
Co-founder and first president of Mattel, she dreamed up a certain doll in 1959 and was later portrayed in the 2023 Barbie film — who was she?
Ruth Handler: American business magnate and inventor (1916–2002)
Named from Greek words for 'thorn' and 'earthworm,' which genus of large tropical centipedes gives its name to an entire family of segmented, many-legged predators?
Despite historians noting that email already existed in the early 1970s, this MIT-trained engineer holds a 1982 copyright and claims to have invented it as a teenager — who is he?
Shiva Ayyadurai: American engineer, conspiracy theorist, and entrepreneur.
Raised in the Bronx by Puerto Rican-born parents after her father's early death, this Princeton and Yale Law graduate became the third woman ever named to the U.S. Supreme Court — who is she?
Sonia Sotomayor: US Supreme Court justice since 2009.

Often triggered by medications like lamotrigine or allopurinol, this severe skin reaction starts with flu-like symptoms before the skin begins to blister, peel, and affect mucous membranes — what is this condition called?
Stevens–Johnson syndrome: Skin disease. The most common cause is certain medications such as lamotrigine, carbamazepine, allopurinol, sulfonamide antibiotics and nevirapine.

This red-orange, sublimable heterocyclic solid is a stable aminoxyl radical used as a spin probe in electron spin resonance spectroscopy and as a mediator in controlled radical polymerization — what's this compound commonly called?

This geometry rule holds that a triangle inscribed in a circle, with one side running through the center as a diameter, always has a right angle at its third point — proved by Euclid, though occasionally miscredited to Pythagoras. What's it called?
Thales's theorem: On triangles inscribed in a circle with a diameter as an edge.

A nightshade cousin of tobacco and chili peppers, its edible berry was carried from western South America to Eurasia by the Spanish during the Columbian exchange — which fruit, eaten as a vegetable, is it?
Tomato: Edible berry. The tomato (US:, UK:; Solanum lycopersicum) is a plant whose fruit is an edible berry that is eaten as a vegetable.
A member of the ginger family native to the Indian subcontinent, its boiled and dried rhizomes are ground into a deep orange-yellow powder used to color and flavor curries — what is it?
